item.title: Sophie Cunningham's insufferable ex-teammate mouths off but can't make a shot, ref lowers his shoulder & Ditka
item.description: Another Friday Nightcaps digs into Sydney Colson's profane rant telling Sophie Cunningham to shut up about transgender athletes, plus her WNBA stats.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

Another Friday. We're here. We've made it!

While the left spent all week whining about Sophie Cunningham's hat and firing squad best practices, us PATRIOTS were biding our time, keeping our heads down, and grinding towards another weekend.

And now, we're here. And there ain't a thing they can do about it.

Let's roll.

Welcome to a Friday Nightcaps — the one where Sophie Cunningham's ex-teammate, Sydney Colson, virtue-signals her BUTT off while also having maybe the worst career stats I've ever seen.

SPORTS MEDIA OUTLET CONSIDERS SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM MORE POLARIZING THAN MEGAN RAPINOE

Seriously. This is who's telling Sophie — and white people — to shut up? The WNBA can do better than this, right?

Right?!

What else? I've got Dak getting heckled by an Uber driver, a referee absolutely trucking a poor soul on the sidelines, and I'm sad about Mike Ditka. What an awful year for deaths.

I feel like we say that every year, but goodness, 2026 has been a real kick to the you-know-whats in terms of death. And we still have three months to go!

Brutal.

On that happy note, grab you a slice of sausage pizza ahead of Sunday's National Sausage Pizza Day, and settle in for a Friday 'Cap!

I've got no real hot takes on pizza beyond the fact that I do, in fact, believe sausage is the best topping. I'm not just saying that because of the occasion. It's the best, by a mile.

Mount Rushmore of Pizza Toppings to kick this Friday class off? Sure. Why not?!

Meatballs as a topping are underrated in the pizza topping game. They're not on every menu, but when they are, HAMMER it. You are welcome!

And that concludes our Ted Talk portion of today's class.

NOW, let's officially get the day started with some ex-WNBA player named Sydney Colson pandering to the left by telling Sophie Cunningham and her white counterparts to PIPE DOWN.

Amazing:

Listen, if you never speak up about a d–n thing when you know it’s impacting the people that you claim to love, care about, you know we’re fighting together as a team, sister, blah blah blah, and you don’t speak up when things affect them. They don’t respect you.

They are just trying to make it.

Let me just tell you now, for real, for real: For the white players in the league, when you don’t say s–t, and even worse, when you say things that are harmful, talking about the trans s–t, nobody respects you. Shut the f–k up. Shut the f–k up. Nobody wants to hear your opinion. Freedom of speech, so you can say it, but just know people are just trying to get by when they’re dealing with you.

And you ought to be ashamed. Y’all ought to be ashamed to act like you’re cool with people, to act like you care about sisterhood, all of these things.

Again, it's just amazing. These "athletes" are just incredible. They're the gifts that keep on giving "the whole year," as Cousin Eddie would say.

As Dan Z. said in the above post, let's quickly remind everyone of the VERY HARMFUL thing Sophie Cunningham told ESPN months ago as it pertains to trans people:

"I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I’m like, ‘I never once said that.’ I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men."

That's it! THAT's what Sydney Colson, who played with Cunningham last season in Indiana, deems "harmful" rhetoric.

Speaking of last season, because I had never heard of this girl before this morning, I decided to do some Big J digging to see if her play on the court warranted all this chest-pumping off of it.

It ... did not:

Well, there you have it. That's who is calling out Sophie Cunningham. A player who struggled to score three points per game during her illustrious career in the WNBA.

Okeedokee!

By the way, for the "Sophie stinks, too!" crowd ... she's averaged at least 8 points per game off the bench every year since 2022, including two seasons in double-digits. She's also a top-five three-point shooter in the league.

It ain't close.

OK, let's rapid-fire this Friday class into a big weekend of FOOTBALL!

To hype everyone up, let's start off with a ref in last night's South Alabama-Arkansas State game lowering his shoulder on a 100-yard kick return:

BOOOOM! You don't often see a referee doing the trucking, right? Usually, we're watching those guys get pummeled. Frankly, it's a nice change of pace for the Zebras. I've spent all year ragging on them — for good reason. They've generally stunk at all levels.

But credit where it's due here. This guy had a job to do, and he wasn't gonna let some innocent bystander stand in his way. Nicely done.

Next? Speaking of (not so) innocent bystanders ...

So, Dak and the Cowboys put up their annual primetime clunker last night, and this was the big story that came out of it ...

Someone — boots on the ground say the guy was a driver — called Dak "embarrassing" after he threw two picks in a loss to the winless Buccaneers, and he took exception to it.

I say fair on both accounts, by the way. The guy was pissed. He was clearly a fan. Dak stunk. It was embarrassing.

Dak also has a right to turn his head around and get pissed. I would, too. And if the guy really did turn his head around after saying it, and then doubled down AFTER Dak looked away, it is kind of a wussy move.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

If you're gonna say something, say it! Don't be a keyboard warrior. Man up, call Dak out for his stinker, and let the chips fall where they may.

OK, that's it for today — and this week. Good work, everyone. Solid week. And now we get to enjoy three straight nights of football.

What a blessing. What a country.

It's only fitting to let the late Mike Ditka take us home.

RIP to a legend.

item.title: John Cena 'got ran out' of Hollywood before unexpected second chance
item.description: John Cena admits he was "ran out of the movie business" for not caring, revealing his heart stayed in the WWE ring during his early Hollywood roles.
item.content:encoded:
John Cena’s Hollywood career nearly ended before it ever truly got off the ground.

The WWE legend admitted he was "ran out of the movie business" because he simply didn’t care enough about acting, revealing that his heart remained in the wrestling ring as he struggled to embrace the slower pace of life on a film set.

Cena reflected on the rocky start to a Hollywood career that would eventually include roles in "The Suicide Squad," the "Fast & Furious" franchise and "Peacemaker" during an appearance on the "Today" show.

SYLVESTER STALLONE'S ADVICE TO THOSE WHO ARE STRUGGLING 50 YEARS AFTER 'ROCKY' CHANGED HIS LIFE

"It’s been a long journey," he explained. "I think that’s the important one. People think things happen overnight. Those early projects – truth be told – I didn’t have my heart into."

For Cena, his priorities were elsewhere.

"As a young 20-something, God, traveling the world, being out in front of tens of thousands of people every night going nuts and then doing it night after night. That’s where I wanted to be, and that’s where I felt comfortable and fluent," he said, referencing his successful career in the WWE.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Cena described working on a film set as "super patient" and "super slow."

"I just didn’t have the wisdom for the process," he claimed.

But Hollywood apparently had little patience for Cena’s lack of enthusiasm.

"I got ran out of the movie business for not caring and that’s justifiably so," he added. "If you don’t care about something, give somebody the opportunity that does."

Cena began his acting career with roles in movies such as "The Marine" and "12 Rounds." However, Cena didn't see success until the 2010s with roles in "Trainwreck," "Blockers" and "The Suicide Squad." 

He's said his role as Peacemaker in the DC Extended Universe changed his life. The 2021 movie has since been turned into a TV series.

Cena also joined the "Fast and Furious" franchise in 2021, playing Vin Diesel's character's brother in "Fast 9: The Fast Saga" and "Fast X." The actor later made a cameo in "Barbie" in 2023 and starred in the Hulu original movies "Vacation Friends" plus "Vacation Friends 2."

But after years of finding his footing in Hollywood, Cena said his attitude toward acting couldn't be more different today.

"I’m now super passionate about what I do, and that’s everything from filming to sitting here talking about this movie with you guys. And I’m so lucky to be given a second chance," he said. "And that took 20 years to craft."

The "Today" hosts also highlighted Cena’s self-awareness as he reflected on how much he has changed over the years.

"Man, I think there’s nothing wrong with taking inventory of yourself, looking in the mirror, loving yourself for your strengths and your flaws and trying to work to be better than you were yesterday," he said.

Cena began his WWE career in 2002 on "Smackdown!" as "The Prototype," eventually transforming into his rapper persona, the "Doctor of Thuganomics."

Throughout his career, Cena has won a record-breaking 17 WWE world championships. He officially retired in 2025.

item.title: Monday Night Football lost half of its audience in one week during Falcons-Saints
item.description: The Falcons-Saints Monday Night Football game drew just 11.9 million viewers, but the Bills-Rams matchup with Josh Allen could deliver a huge rebound.
item.content:encoded:
On Monday, the Falcons-Saints matchup drew about as small an audience as a national Primetime NFL game can draw in 2026.

The game averaged just 11.9 million viewers across ABC, ESPN, ESPN2, and ESPN Deportes.

For context, the Week 3 Monday night game between the Eagles and Bears drew 22.6 million viewers, nearly double the audience.

A week-over-week decline of roughly 50% is rare. But the disparity also illustrates why neither ESPN nor the NFL should be particularly concerned about Monday's unusually poor number.

Through the first three weeks of the season, Monday Night Football had averaged 21.8 million viewers. Monday's game dropped the season average to 19.325 million.

WWE'S MICHAEL COLE REFUSES TO DIP HIS TOE INTO POLITICAL WATERS, BUCKING TREND AMONG SPORTS BROADCASTERS

The decline is almost certainly attributable to the matchup and the game itself. Neither the Falcons nor the Saints is much of a national draw in its current form. Perhaps Michael Penix Jr. and Tyler Shough will become attractions. Today, they are not.

It was also an ugly and largely uncompetitive game, with Atlanta ultimately winning 45-24.

The NFL and ESPN likely knew this wouldn't be a marquee matchup. Instead, they marketed the night around the 20th anniversary of the Saints' return to the Superdome after Hurricane Katrina. In that 2006 game, New Orleans defeated Atlanta after Steve Gleason blocked a punt in one of the defining moments in franchise history, a play now immortalized with a statue outside the stadium.

The pregame commemoration of that anniversary was well done, even if more fans than usual skipped the game that followed.

Looking ahead, ESPN should have no such concerns this coming Monday. The network will broadcast the most intriguing matchup of Week 5, and perhaps of the season so far, when the Bills visit the Rams.

Buffalo and Los Angeles are the two leading Super Bowl favorites, and Josh Allen and Matthew Stafford are widely considered two of the best quarterbacks in the NFL. Patrick Mahomes, of course, remains firmly in that discussion.

THESE 6 NFL TEAMS ARE FIRMLY IN THE SUPER BOWL BUBBLE THROUGH WEEK 4

If the game stays competitive, the Bills-Rams could surpass the 22.6 million viewers who watched Eagles-Bears two weeks earlier.

There is one complicating factor, however: the MLB postseason. Both League Championship Series will play Monday. Dodgers-Brewers begins at 5 p.m. ET on Fox, while Rays-Cleveland/Chicago begins at 8 p.m. on TBS.

The NFL game will undoubtedly top the baseball games in overall viewership, but the competition could prevent the Rams-Bills from reaching heights it could otherwise.

Interestingly, NBC will air the Falcons in Primetime this weekend against the Baltimore Ravens.

On Friday, the Ravens ruled out quarterback Lamar Jackson. The quarterback duo of Penix vs. Tyler "Snoop" Huntley is arguably worse than what ESPN aired this past Monday. And the NBC game will air head-to-head with Game 1 of the highly anticipated Dodgers-Brewers series.

Monday Night Football should top Sunday Night Football this week by a notable margin.

item.title: WWE's Michael Cole may have no idea the outcome of major matches like Money in the Bank ahead of time
item.description: Michael Cole reveals he often doesn't know WWE match outcomes, including this weekend's Money in the Bank ladder match event in New Orleans.
item.content:encoded:
The pro wrestling matches are famously pre-determined. Everyone who tunes into events – small or large – knows that the outcome of the match has already been decided. But that doesn’t necessarily mean everyone knows who is going to win or lose at all times.

Viewers certainly don’t know. They may have an inkling of who would win based on the story places like WWE want to tell, but nothing is ever 100% certain. Now, how about the broadcasters? A viewer may anticipate that those calling the match, like Michael Cole, already know whose hand is going to be raised at the end of the match. But that’s not always the case.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

Cole explained in an interview with OutKick’s Bobby Burack for OutKick Dropkick that he doesn’t like to know what the outcome is going to be sometimes, especially in unique matches like this weekend’s Money in the Bank. Men and women will participate in separate matches and try to climb the ladder to earn a future shot at a world title.

"Fifty-fifty. Sometimes I do because I need to know where to lead the audience in terms of where stories may be going each and every week," Cole said of knowing the result of the matches. "Of course, we’re episodic TV. We need to be able to explain to the audience where we’re going each and every week.

"Sometimes, I don’t like to know the ending of matches. The Money in the Bank match is a great example. I want the excitement to take over. There have been some great matches over the years where I didn’t know the finish for: The Undertaker vs. Brock Lesnar when Brock Lesnar defeated Undertaker and ended his undefeated streak at WrestleMania. I didn’t know that was going to happen. I didn’t know that Seth Rollins was going to cash in the Money in the Bank at WrestleMania. ‘Heist of the Century’ I came up with on the fly."

The Money in the Bank premium live event is highly anticipated by fans each year. Everyone wants to know who is going to get that push and earn an opportunity for a world title shot.

The men’s match includes: CM Punk, Kevin Owens, Trick Williams, Bron Breakker, Je’Von Evans and Penta. The women’s match includes: Sol Ruca, Lola Vice, Jacy Jayne, Roxanne Perez, Lash Legend and Tiffany Stratton.

Cole ranked Money in the Bank somewhere around the level of two other major premium live events.

"Money in the Bank, for us, is right up there. Almost at the same level as the Royal Rumble, Survivor Series," he said. "Not quite WrestleMania or SummerSlam, but it’s getting there. It’s such an important part of our calendar because it’s an opportunity for a man and a woman to change their entire career and change their lives.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"When you climb the ladder and grab the briefcase, a contract is inside that you can cash in for a title opportunity whenever you want it. And this year’s field is so great. There’s some veterans. There’s a lot of rookies. So it’s going to be amazing to see who has an opportunity to really change their life around."

Cole said, for the most part, he won’t know the winners of the event and he will have to come up with the perfect line on the fly which will forever be cemented in the winners’ legacy.

"Money in the Bank is really unique because ladder matches are a very difficult match to call because the action is nonstop," he explained. "There’s really no rest period for us to really be able to tell stories or develop our characters. It’s really pedal to the metal, go, go, go, from the time the bell rings. We do a lot of our work during the entrances. We try to explain to people who some of these superstars are. It’s very important because we have a new audience each and every time that we have a premium live event. It’s important that we bring our characters forward.

"This year’s Money in the Bank ladder match, both on the men’s and on the women’s sides, have a lot of newcomers. So, we’re really going to have to do our job in the entrances of explaining to people who these characters are and why they should have an emotional connection to them. That’s a big part of this. And again, of course, there’s the ending. The person who finally climbs the ladder and grabs the briefcase. How can you make that moment different? How can you make that moment special? And that’s my job."

Money in the Bank takes place at the Smoothie King Center in New Orleans on Saturday. The event begins at 6 p.m. ET.

item.title: Fugitive Ryan Hanafin, wanted after mother found dead in kitchen, waives extradition
item.description: Ryan Hanafin waived extradition in a brief Vermont hearing, agreeing to return to Massachusetts after his mother Andria Hanafin was found shot dead.
item.content:encoded:
BARRE, Vt. — The 22-year-old Massachusetts man arrested in Vermont Thursday hours after his mother was found shot dead in her kitchen has waived extradition and agreed to be returned to his home state.

Ryan Hanafin was the subject of an interstate manhunt Thursday after his 48-year-old father Matthew Hanafin arrived home around 12:38 a.m. and found his wife, 49-year-old Andria Hanafin, shot dead in their kitchen in Reading, Massachusetts, according to Middlesex County District Attorney Marian Ryan.

The local prosecutor said in court that she had spoken with Massachusetts State Police and expected them to be able to retrieve Ryan Hanafin "pretty quickly" in a brief hearing Friday afternoon.

RYAN HANAFIN ARRESTED IN VERMONT AFTER MOM ANDRIA FOUND DEAD OF GUNSHOT WOUND IN MASSACHUSETTS HOME

In a hearing where both the judge and defendant appeared virtually, with only the lawyers and media in the courtroom, Hanafin answered "Yes sir," when asked if he could hear the judge.

Hanafin was wearing a blue protective covering over his chest and shoulders as he appeared remotely.

SEND US A TIP

"You are charged with crimes, felony crimes, in the state of Massachusetts, and they would like to have you returned," the judge said. "You have the right to go through what is called the formal governor's warrant process, and that's where the governor of Massachusetts formally asks the governor of Vermont to surrender you, and that takes some time, and they have to make sure that their paperwork is correct, then they would send you back."

The judge added that he could file a habeas petition and challenge the state's authority to hold him in the meantime.

"The most common basis for that might be that you were the wrong Ryan Hanafin," the judge said. "By waiving extradition, you're giving up your opportunity to go through the governor's warrant process and file any habeas petition. Do you understand that?"

"Yes sir," Hanafin replied.

The judge asked if he had taken any drugs or had any mental conditions that would affect his judgment or make it difficult to understand the proceedings.

"No sir," Hanafin replied to each question.

He said he had spoken with his attorney and understood his advice.

"All right," the judge continued, "is it your voluntary choice to waive extradition and return to Massachusetts?"

"Yes, that's what I'd like to do," Hanafin replied.

Timing for his return to Massachusetts to face charges in Reading, where his mother was shot to death, was not immediately clear.

The judge set a status conference for next Thursday to make sure Hanafin's transfer had been completed.

"We'll set it for status next Thursday just to make sure Massachusetts has retrieved him, and if they haven't yet, we'll ask for some status report on that," he said.

The entire hearing lasted roughly four minutes.

Reading police have so far called him a person of interest and not a suspect, and authorities have not publicly identified the Massachusetts felony charges referenced during Friday's extradition hearing.

Vermont state troopers were on the lookout for his black Dodge Charger in Warren, Vermont, where he had known ties. About two hours into their search, they found him, and he was arrested without incident, authorities said.

item.title: Women's college basketball player released from ICE custody, details conditions: 'Just me and myself'
item.description: Kentucky State University's Aminata Seck says she spent a week in isolation in ICE custody after refusing to remove a knee brace for her torn ACL.
item.content:encoded:
A Kentucky State University women's basketball player was released on bond from ICE custody after two months.

Aminata Seck, a Senegal native, was arrested on Aug. 7 at Louisville Muhammad Ali International Airport after the Department of Homeland Security said she "chose to overstay her welcome in violation of our nation’s laws." She entered legally in 2019 "on a temporary basis," and DHS, which referred to Seck as an "illegal alien," said she missed an immigration hearing in September 2025, leading to a judge ordering her removal.

An immigration judge set her bond at $2,500, and she is now home.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Seck is currently dealing with a torn ACL and meniscus and was slated for surgery, but it was postponed while she was in custody. At a news conference, Seck's attorney, Sadiqa Reynolds, said she "did not regularly receive treatment in custody."

"It is a longstanding practice to provide comprehensive medical care from the moment an alien enters ICE custody. This includes medical, dental, and mental health services as available, and access to medical appointments and 24-hour emergency care. Illegal aliens also have access to phones to communicate with their family members and lawyers. This is the best healthcare than many aliens have received in their lives," DHS said to Fox News Digital.

Seck said she spent a week in isolation because she refused to remove a knee brace she was wearing to treat the injury.

"By myself in that room, with nobody — just me and myself, looking at the wall, no books or anything," Seck said at the conference, via KFVS.

SHAQ URGES FEVER STAR TO CASH IN BY EMBRACING CAITLIN CLARK FANDOM AFTER ALARMING COMMENTS

Kentucky State University and ICE did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

"She has no criminal record, but ICE grabbed her from her team and threw her in a jail cell for two months," U.S. Rep. Morgan McGarvey, D-Ky., said at the conference.

"Being in detention is a choice. We encourage all illegal aliens to take control of their departure with the CBP Home App. The United States is offering illegal aliens $3,000 and a free flight to self-deport now. We encourage every person here illegally to take advantage of this offer and reserve the chance to come back to the U.S. the right legal way to live the American dream. If not, you will be arrested and deported without a chance to return," DHS said.

Seck played in 20 games last season, starting in 17 of them, and averaged 11.9 points and 7.7 rebounds per game.

"I'm just ready to go back to school, get my master's and get this surgery done," Seck said at the conference.

Her immigration case is ongoing, and she is expected to be back in court next month.

item.title: Massive 7.7 magnitude earthquake strikes Panama as officials investigate potential tsunami threat
item.description: A powerful earthquake struck Panama's southern coast Friday, prompting officials to investigate a possible tsunami threat after the USGS lowered its magnitude estimate from 8.0 to 7.7.
item.content:encoded:
A powerful 7.7 magnitude earthquake struck off Panama's southern coast Friday, shaking the country's capital as officials investigated a potential tsunami threat. 

The U.S. Geological Survey initially measured the earthquake at magnitude 8.0 before lowering its estimate to 7.7. The quake struck at 1:56 p.m. ET, approximately 6 miles beneath the surface, near Pitaloza Arriba, Panama.

A 5.5 magnitude aftershock followed, with its epicenter approximately 50 miles east of the initial earthquake.

The earthquake was felt in Panama City and in San José, the capital of neighboring Costa Rica, according to Reuters.

item.title: Furious suburban millionaires say luxury helicopters are ruining their peace
item.description: Residents of New York City suburbs say low-flying helicopters ferrying the ultra-rich to the Hamptons are shattering their peace on busy travel weekends.
item.content:encoded:
Residents of some leafy New York City suburbs say their peace and quiet is being shattered by helicopters ferrying even wealthier travelers out to the Hamptons, according to new reporting. 

Homeowners along Westchester County's Sound Shore have complained about low-flying helicopters passing over communities, including Larchmont and Mamaroneck, especially during the warmer months as the ultra rich flock to the popular eastern Long Island getaway, The Wall Street Journal recently reported.

"I have to put the closed captions on so I can see what's happening on the screen," Larchmont resident Jay Davis, a Realtor and attorney, told the Journal about helicopters interrupting television and conversations at his home. 

AIR TAXIS CUT HOUR-LONG COMMUTES TO MINUTES, RIDERS MAY BE SHOCKED BY THE PRICE

"I don't want to continue to live like this." 

Longtime resident Nancy Monzidelis told the outlet the aircraft can sound startlingly close.

"One time I thought I had a helicopter in my driveway," she said. "It's not as peaceful as it was before."

The dispute has created a clash between the ultra-wealthy and the not-quite-as-wealthy, the Journal noted. 

Larchmont and Mamaroneck homes can command seven-figure prices, according to real estate sales data. 

ONCE-AFFORDABLE SUMMER ESCAPE ROCKED BY SOARING COSTS AS FAMILIES SHELL OUT THOUSANDS

Celebrities, including Joan Rivers, Matt Dillon and Lou Gehrig have all had ties to the two towns.

Some operators advertise seats starting at $795 each way, while private charters can start at more than $4,700 and unlimited summer passes can go for $25,000, according to their websites.

Some residents told the Journal the helicopter traffic has been especially noticeable on summer Fridays and Sundays as travelers head east for the weekend and then return to the city.

Patrick Bucquet, a Mamaroneck resident, told the outlet that helicopters can pass overhead as frequently as every 15 minutes during busy periods.

"Maybe some people are doing very well, so they can afford a helicopter. Good for them," he said.

"Of course, they can travel to the Hamptons," he added. "But maybe they can take another route."

item.title: Marco Rubio announces sweeping financial sanctions against the International Criminal Court
item.description: Marco Rubio announced the Trump administration will soon freeze ICC assets and bar all U.S. transactions with the International Criminal Court.
item.content:encoded:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced Friday that the Trump administration is imposing sweeping financial sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC), a body the president has sought to dismantle throughout his second term.

To date, the administration has sanctioned 17 individuals with ties to the ICC, including judges and prosecutors. The latest move marks the first time the U.S. has gone after the institution itself.

"Our message is clear: The United States and the American people are not subject to the jurisdiction of this fake ICC," Rubio said in a pre-recorded video message released Friday morning. "Both parties agree on this, but only President Trump has the resolve to take the action needed to end this threat once and for all."

This comes hours after this year's Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Navanethem "Navi" Pillay, a former ICC judge.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION SANCTIONS SITTING PRESIDENT OF THE INTERNATIONAL CRIMINAL COURT FOR 'ABUSES OF POWER'

In a statement Friday, the Netherlands-based court strongly condemned the U.S. sanctions as "an assault on the rule of law and on the very foundations of the international legal order."

"This measure targets an independent judicial institution, created by treaty and entrusted by 125 States Parties with investigating and prosecuting genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and the crime of aggression," the ICC added.

"It is an attempt to obstruct the course of justice and to prevent the Court from doing what it was created to do."

ICC President Tomoko Akane, who was personally sanctioned by the Trump administration in August, said the court will continue to operate despite the new penalties.

In announcing the sanctions, Rubio argued the ICC believes it has the authority to prosecute American service members operating overseas and even U.S. Border Patrol agents. There is no evidence the court has sought to investigate or prosecute Border Patrol agents, though Rubio previously raised that possibility in July.

WORLD COURT PROSECUTOR WHO WENT AFTER NETANYAHU FOR WAR CRIMES SUSPENDED OVER SEXUAL MISCONDUCT

The administration's concerns about U.S. personnel are not entirely hypothetical. In 2017, an ICC prosecutor sought authorization to investigate alleged war crimes committed by U.S. military and intelligence personnel in Afghanistan.

ICC judges initially rejected the request, but that decision was overturned on appeal in 2020, allowing the investigation to proceed. The court's prosecutor later de-prioritized alleged crimes involving U.S. personnel to focus on alleged crimes committed by the Taliban and ISIS-K.

Under the new sanctions, any ICC assets subject to U.S. jurisdiction will be frozen, while Americans, U.S. businesses and banks are generally barred from conducting transactions with the court.

The sanctions will not go into effect immediately. The Treasury Department has given the ICC a 180-day general license to maintain its operations, giving the court time to address U.S. concerns.

ICC TURNS 'BLIND EYE' TO TOP WORLD THREATS WHILE TARGETING AMERICANS, TRUMP ADMIN SAYS

"Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC. And we expect our allies, many of whom are part of the ICC and that rely on American service members for their defense, to rein in this rogue court," Rubio said.

"If they do not, the United States will continue its campaign to dismantle the ICC piece by piece until Americans are threatened no longer."

One of the other major grievances the administration has with the ICC is its decision to issue arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Defense Minister Yoav Gallant in 2024.

The ICC argued both officials were responsible for war crimes and crimes against humanity against Palestinians in Gaza during Israel's military response to the Hamas-led Oct. 7 terrorist attacks in 2023. Both men have denied wrongdoing.

In a February 2025 executive order authorizing sanctions against ICC officials, President Donald Trump called the arrest warrants "baseless" and said the court overstepped its authority since Israel was not an ICC member.

The ICC maintains that it can exercise jurisdiction over nationals of non-member states when they are accused of qualifying crimes committed on the territory of a state that has accepted the court’s jurisdiction.

item.title: Dem scrambles to change tune on trans athletes as Trump targets past record: ‘Annie Trannie’
item.description: South Carolina U.S. Senate candidate Annie Andrews claims she was misrepresented on transgender sports after Trump dubbed her "Annie Trannie."
item.content:encoded:
A South Carolina Democrat running for U.S. Senate who previously opposed legislation restricting transgender athletes' participation in girls' sports is now emphasizing her opposition to biological males participating in female athletics as President Donald Trump targets her record ahead of the midterm elections.

Trump took aim at Annie Andrews, a pediatrician challenging Republican Sen. Darline Graham, in a series of Truth Social posts this week, dubbing her "Annie Trannie" and accusing her of supporting transgender policies that are out of step with South Carolina voters.

The president also shared an attack ad accusing Andrews of supporting biological males competing against female athletes. "Annie Andrews is for they/them, not for our values, not for South Carolina," the ad said.

But Andrews pushed back in an interview with Fox News Digital on Thursday, arguing that her positions have been misrepresented.

"I don't support biological men playing in women's sports and I don't support gender surgery on minors," Andrews said.

Her comments stand in contrast to her public opposition to South Carolina's 2022 Save Women’s Sports Act, which restricted transgender athletes' participation in girls' and women's school sports. At the time, Andrews called the legislation "shameful" and "actively harmful," raising questions about how she reconciles her past opposition to the law with her current campaign position.

DEMOCRATS ARE CHANGING THEIR TRANSGENDER MESSAGE. REPUBLICANS SAY THEY’RE JUST FLIP-FLOPPING

As passed, the bill required interscholastic, intercollegiate, intramural and club teams sponsored by public schools and colleges to be designated as male or female-coded. It then closed women’s teams to male students and similarly closed men’s sports to women — unless the school did not have a designated women’s team. Private schools competing against public schools were required to follow the same rules.

It also allowed students harmed by a violation to sue schools.

Andrews’ social media post at the time garnered resurfaced attention as she launched her 2026 Senate bid, attracting pressure from Republicans.

"Annie "Trannie" Andrews is running against our wonderful Darline Graham for the Senate in South Carolina," Trump wrote in one post.

"Annie Trannie is not, in particular, as it pertains to representing the Values of the Great People of South Carolina — She is in favor of Transgender for Everyone, Open Borders, Defunding the Police, High Taxes, a Weak Military, and will absolutely fight to take your guns away — In other words, she is against our Great Second Amendment! Trannie is not for South Carolina, and South Carolina must show, in the upcoming Election, that it is not for her," Trump added.

In her interview with Fox News Digital, Andrews dismissed Trump's barb, calling it a distraction from the issues central to voters in South Carolina.

"And in regards to the name-calling, if calling me names is going to lower gas and diesel prices here for so many hardworking South Carolinian families, if it’s going to lower grocery prices or somehow make healthcare more affordable then he can call me all the names he wants but I don’t think that’s a path to solution so I’m going to stay focused on what I can do to help folks in South Carolina," Andrews said.

Andrews did not immediately respond to additional requests for comment on whether her statements reflected a change in stance. She also did not expand on what had drawn criticism for the Save Women’s Sports Act.

TALARICO CAMP SAYS HE OPPOSES TRANS ATHLETES IF UNSAFE OR UNFAIR BUT ACCUSES POLITICIANS OF BULLYING STUDENTS

At least one Republican onlooker, National Republican Senatorial Regional Press Secretary Nick Puglia, believes her remarks speaks poorly of the message she's presenting to voters.

"Annie Andrews' blatant lies show just how desperate she is and how little she thinks of South Carolinians. But nothing Andrews says or does will change her far-left record," Puglia said in a comment.

This isn't the first time Andrews has received Republican criticisms for what they view as retreats from trans policies. In 2022, Rep. Nancy Mace, R-S.C., called out Andrews for, in her view, trying to walk back her opposition to H. 4047, a bill that would "prohibit the performance of a medical procedure or the prescription or issuance of medication, upon or to a minor, that is intended to alter the appearance of the minor's gender or delay puberty, with exceptions; to create criminal penalties; and for other purposes."

Andrews said she opposed the bill in a post to X, calling it "dangerous," only to later say that she opposed trans procedures for minors.

"She called thewww.youtube.comwww.youtube.com legislation to ban that kind of surgery dangerous. She called that legislation an attack on our youth. And it wasn't until we called her out on it that she decided that she's now not for something that she was very publicly in support of just last year. And so it's really hard to play hide and seek from your public comments, because once you tweet it, it's on their public record forever. And that's how we discovered it," Mace told Fox News Digital at the time.

Notably, she isn’t the only Democrat who in recent weeks has received attention for seeming shifts in her position over transgender policies. Fellow Democrats like Rep. Marcy Kaptur, D-Ohio, Rep. Don Davis, D-N.C., and Sarah Trone Garriott, a congressional candidate in Iowa, have all been forced to reiterate their positions as Republicans have highlighted their records on the subject.

WATCH: BATTLEGROUND DEMOCRAT CALLED IOWA A 'BACKWATER' OVER TRANSGENDER ATHLETES BAN

In Kaptur’s case, she described how she had "voted with Republicans to keep transgender ideology out of our schools" despite voting against a women’s sports bill. Similarly, Davis voted "present" on that same women’s bill while later claiming that women should have "safe and fair space" in sports. And Garriott, who cast a vote against a ban on biological men in women’s locker rooms, clarified her stance earlier this year, stating that "I oppose letting men in women’s locker rooms."

Those statements reflect broader trends in public opinion showing consensus on trans athlete policies.

Recently, the Pew Research Center found in a Aug. 11 report that 73% of respondents were "not at all" or "not too" comfortable with "athletes competing on sports teams that do not match their sex at birth," compared to just 13% that replied that they were "extremely" or "very" comfortable with the idea. Similarly, 66% of participants said they would support laws or policies requiring trans athletes to compete on teams that match their biological sex compared to 15% who said they would oppose such policies.

With just four weeks left to address criticisms over her views, Andrews now heads to South Carolina’s general election on Nov. 3., having cleared the state's Democratic primary earlier this year in June.

item.title: One type of sleep linked to dramatically lower risk of dementia, Parkinson's and 81 other diseases
item.description: Greater REM sleep was linked to 80% lower Parkinson's risk and 46% lower dementia risk in a major study of over 95,000 adults tracked for years.
item.content:encoded:
Not all stages of sleep are equal in terms of benefits for the brain.

Greater amounts of rapid eye movement (REM) sleep were associated with lower risks of 83 diseases, including dementia, Parkinson’s disease and heart failure, new research has shown.

Additionally, greater amounts of deep sleep were associated with lower risks of seven conditions.

THIS ONE QUESTION MAY REVEAL WHETHER YOUR BODY IS GETTING THE REST IT NEEDS, STUDY FINDS

That’s according to a study of 95,559 adults who wore wrist accelerometers continuously for seven consecutive days and nights. Researchers in China used deep-learning algorithms to analyze REM sleep, deep sleep, light sleep, total sleep duration, wakefulness after sleep onset and sleep irregularity.

They then looked at health records to assess associations with more than 1,000 diseases over a nearly nine-year follow-up period.

Greater REM sleep was associated with a significantly lower risk of several diseases, including Parkinson’s (80% lower relative risk), dementia (46% lower risk) and heart failure (26% lower risk).

Greater deep sleep was associated with lower risks of seven conditions, including Type 2 diabetes and major depressive disorder.

MORE NAPS, HIGHER RISK? RESEARCH LINKS DAYTIME SLEEP TO HEALTH WARNINGS IN AGING ADULTS

Sleep duration was also found to be highly linked to disease outcome. Six to eight hours per night was found to be the "sweet spot" associated with the lowest risk for 69 diseases. In contrast, sleeping fewer than five hours per night was linked to an increased risk of 37 health conditions.

The study also found that greater night-to-night sleep irregularity and more wakefulness during the night were associated with higher risks of several conditions, including anxiety and substance use disorders.

The findings were published Sept. 17 in the journal PLOS Medicine.

"I think what is important is the total duration of sleep, and the percentage that REM takes up," Oki Ishikawa, M.D., pulmonary, critical care and sleep medicine expert at Northwell’s Northern Westchester Hospital, told Fox News Digital.

"The average percentage of REM sleep in this study population was about 20%, and generally 20-25% is considered normal per sleep cycle."

5-STEP SLEEP RESET COULD PROMOTE HEALTHY WEIGHT LOSS, NUTRITIONIST SAYS

Ishikawa, who was not involved in the study, said he does not believe that a higher amount of REM sleep alone will necessarily lower the risk.

"Normal sleep pattern and duration are associated with aspects like maintenance of good immune function and memory, so I think the important message here is to try and get a sufficient amount of sleep in general," Ishikawa sai. 

Disrupted sleep may sometimes be an early warning sign of disease rather than simply a cause, according to Dr. Chelsie Rohrscheib, head sleep expert at Wesper, a sleep analysis company in New York.

"Conditions such as Parkinson’s disease, dementia and heart failure can begin affecting sleep years before they are diagnosed," Rohrscheib, who also was not involved in the research, told Fox News Digital.

"At the same time, poor sleep may contribute to disease progression, so the relationship likely works both ways."

DIETITIAN REVEALS SIMPLE EATING STRATEGY FOR BETTER SLEEP — AND ONE HABIT TO AVOID

The researchers noted some limitations of the study. Because it was observational, it could only show an association and could not prove that increasing REM or deep sleep directly prevents disease.

"Sleep was measured for only one week using a wrist device, which is less accurate than a clinical sleep study for identifying sleep stages," Rohrscheib said.

"Some health information was collected years earlier, medications that can affect sleep were not fully considered and some medical diagnoses may have been missed."

As the participants were all from the UK Biobank, the study population was also less diverse and generally healthier than the overall population, so the findings may not apply equally to everyone, Rohrscheib noted.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"Overall, changes in sleep may provide important clues about underlying health, but this study cannot determine whether poor sleep is a cause, an early symptom or both," she concluded.

Rohrscheib also cautioned that while wrist-worn sleep trackers are generally good at estimating sleep stages, they are not 100% accurate.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"Without a formal in-lab sleep study, it's impossible to know how much time the participants spent in REM and other sleep stages," she said.

More research is needed to determine whether increasing REM or deep sleep can help prevent certain diseases, the researchers said.

Future studies could also explore whether the relationship between sleep stages and disease risk varies by age, sex, overall health and other individual characteristics.

Both experts recommended following general sleep hygiene practices, such as maintaining an optimal environment (dark, cool and quiet), keeping a consistent sleep schedule and avoiding sleep-disrupting substances such as alcohol and caffeine.

"If you have other sleep pathologies like sleep apnea … treating that would be a great way to optimize the amount of REM sleep," Ishikawa advised.

While it can be difficult to measure REM sleep without a wearable, he said the best gauge is whether one feels refreshed upon waking and doesn’t feel sleepy during the day.

"If you get about seven to nine hours of uninterrupted sleep, you most likely have the opportunity to cycle through REM in a sufficient way."

item.title: Who is Navi Pillay? Nobel Peace Prize winner's UN record renews fierce antisemitism accusations
item.description: Navi Pillay's 2026 Nobel Peace Prize sparked backlash from Jewish advocacy groups and UN Watch over allegations of anti-Israel bias and antisemitism.
item.content:encoded:
The decision to award the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize to former U.N. human rights chief Navi Pillay sparked fierce backlash Friday from Jewish advocacy groups and U.N. watchdogs accusing the South African jurist of longstanding anti-Israel bias and defending antisemitic rhetoric.

The Norwegian Nobel Committee honored Pillay, 85, for her contributions to international law and efforts to hold perpetrators of war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide accountable.

But her selection immediately reignited controversies surrounding her leadership of U.N. investigations into Israel, her defense of a fellow commissioner accused of antisemitism and positions she expressed before being appointed to investigate the Jewish state.

ICC PROSECUTOR WHOSE NETANYAHU WARRANT FUELED MAMDANI ARREST THREAT IS FIRED OVER SEXUAL MISCONDUCT

"Navi Pillay is indeed a world leader, an individual at the forefront of the international spread of the poisonous forms of antisemitism that beset the 21st century," Anne Bayefsky, president of Human Rights Voices and director of the Touro Institute on Human Rights, told Fox News Digital.

Bayefsky accused Pillay of having "perfected the art of perverting legal and universal standards of human rights to demonize and delegitimize Jewish self-determination. This award stands as a testament to human wrongs."

The Nobel Committee offered a sharply different assessment of Pillay's legacy, praising her lifelong commitment to international justice and describing her career as an example of courage and integrity in defending the rule of law.

ISRAEL VINDICATED BY GAZA NUTRITION DATA AFTER ‘BLOOD LIBEL’ STARVATION CLAIMS, UN ENVOY SAYS

Born in Durban, South Africa, in 1941, Pillay built her career challenging apartheid-era discrimination, becoming the first non-White woman appointed to South Africa's high court. She later served as a judge at the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda and the International Criminal Court.

From 2008 to 2014, she served as U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights. In 2021, she was appointed to chair the U.N. Human Rights Council's open-ended Commission of Inquiry investigating alleged violations in Israel and the Palestinian territories.

In September 2025, the commission concluded that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza, a finding Israel rejected as politically motivated and biased. The commission's conclusion was not a ruling by an international court.

Geneva-based UN Watch condemned Friday's Nobel announcement, accusing Pillay of breaching the impartiality expected of international investigators.

UN CHIEF BACKS OFFICIAL WHO REPOSTED ANTI-ISRAEL ACTIVIST'S CLAIMS AMID CALLS FOR INVESTIGATION

"We are shocked that the Nobel Committee honored Navi Pillay," Executive Director Hillel Neuer said. "Her troubling record on antisemitism and gross breach of ethics in presiding over a notorious U.N. commission utterly disqualifies her from such an award."

Neuer pointed to a June 2020 manifesto that Pillay signed calling on governments to "Sanction Apartheid Israel," along with a June 2021 letter urging President Joe Biden to punish Israel after its conflict with Hamas.

UN Watch argued that the positions raised questions about her impartiality before she accepted the commission's chairmanship in July 2021.

U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres offered a sharply different assessment Friday, congratulating Pillay on the Nobel Peace Prize and praising her decades-long career in international justice, including her leadership of the U.N. investigation into Israel.

"For decades, she has been a champion of international law and human rights and a steadfast, independent voice of justice amidst some of the most historic international legal cases of our time," Guterres said in a statement.

Guterres highlighted her different roles, including chairing the commission investigating Israel and the Palestinian territories, declaring that Pillay had demonstrated "that the force of law must prevail over the law of force and that defending human rights is the surest safeguard against injustice."

NORWAY FACES BACKLASH OVER 'DEEPLY RACIST' PROPOSAL TO JAIL CITIZENS FOR WEST BANK BUSINESS

Another controversy erupted in 2022 when fellow commissioner Miloon Kothari suggested that social media criticism of the investigation was controlled by the "Jewish lobby" and questioned Israel's U.N. membership.

The remarks were condemned by U.S. officials, including then-State Department antisemitism envoy Deborah Lipstadt. Pillay defended Kothari, arguing his comments had been taken out of context. Kothari subsequently apologized, calling his language inappropriate and insensitive.

The controversy also reached Germany, where Berlin's mayor withdrew support for a planned event honoring Pillay in 2022, and the event was canceled, according to The Times of Israel.

Bayefsky also recalled the 2009 U.N. anti-racism conference in Geneva, when Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad delivered an inflammatory speech attacking Israel. While Western diplomats walked out, Pillay remained seated.

However, Pillay subsequently condemned his address, saying she joined the secretary-general in "utterly deploring the speech," according to the U.N.'s official transcript.

"Her after-the-fact denunciation was utterly disingenuous." Bayefsky claimed, "Pillay had been given Ahmadinejad’s speech, questioning the veracity of the Holocaust and talking about the "ugly faces" of Zionists, in advance and yet still handed him the microphone as Conference Secretary-General."

The Nobel Committee, meanwhile, defended Pillay's legacy, crediting her with strengthening international law at a time when the institutions responsible for enforcing it face increasing political pressure.

Pillay's selection highlights the divide between supporters who celebrate her contributions to international justice and critics who contend that her record on Israel undermines the universal human rights principles she championed.

Fox News Digital reached out to Pillay for comment but didn’t receive one in time for publication.

item.title: A'ja Wilson and Breanna Stewart set to headline must-win WNBA playoff games Tuesday night
item.description: The WNBA Playoffs reach a critical point as Angel Reese's Dream and the Valkyries look to close out the Liberty and Aces in must-win Game 3s.
item.content:encoded:
With just four teams remaining in the WNBA Playoffs, we are nearing the finish line. For two of those teams, the Liberty and Aces, the end of the road could be even closer. Both of them face a 0-2 deficit in their series and now must win three straight games if they want to keep their season and championship hopes alive.

The Dream and Valkyries come into tonight with a chance to close out their series, but they must do it on the road as a visiting team.

Let's take a look at both games and see how we should bet on them.

ATLANTA DREAM ADVANCE TO WNBA PLAYOFFS SEMIFINALS FOR FIRST TIME SINCE 2018 WITH GAME 2 WIN

It is a bit hard to believe the Dream are even in this position. They were terrible two years ago. Last year, they improved, but didn't win a playoff series. This season, they went out and traded for Angel Reese, and she rewarded them by winning the WNBA Defensive Player of the Year Award. I genuinely like Reese, but she didn't even lead her team, let alone the league, in steals or blocks.

She did lead them in turnovers and fouls, so I'm not really sure how she won the award. Either way, the team has improved overall with her on the roster and has won four straight playoff games.

The New York Liberty were the preseason favorites to win the championship, but they struggled to get things going this season. They came into the playoffs as the lowest-ranked team, but they did upset the top team, the Lynx.

Game 1 saw them lose by 10, and Game 2 saw them lose by three in overtime. Breanna Stewart continues to be dominant, and Sabrina Ionescu led the way in Game 1, but they need to both be on if they want to stop this Dream attack. Now that the series is shifting to New York, the team should get a bit of a boost, and I think they will win this one. The Liberty are a team of champions and won't go out without a fight. Give me the Liberty -2.5.

The Golden State Valkyries looked anything but dominant in their playoff opener, but they've looked amazing since. I wrote recently about how the Valkyries needed someone to be the "go-to" player instead of the committee approach. It seems like Gabby Williams has listened to those words. She has averaged 24 points per game in the playoffs. In the two wins over the Aces, she has scored 45 points, grabbed 16 rebounds, and dished out eight assists.

If any team in the league knows about having a go-to player, it is the Aces. Las Vegas has the best player in the league, perhaps of all time, in A'ja Wilson. She just won her fifth MVP award and is forgoing the ceremony to focus on tonight's game. Wilson has put up 24 points in both of the games against the Valkyries, but it hasn't been enough. Wilson will be ready for this one, and her team will almost certainly play better at home. I'm going to take the Aces to cover the short -3.5 spread. I also think Wilson will score over 27.5 points tonight.

item.title: Erika Kirk says presidential library-style tribute to Charlie Kirk is 'in the works' as TPUSA expands
item.description: Erika Kirk said a presidential library-style tribute to Charlie Kirk is in the works as TPUSA expands across high school and college campuses.
item.content:encoded:
Erika Kirk says plans for a permanent memorial honoring her late husband, Charlie Kirk, are "in the works" as she oversees what the organization describes as Turning Point USA's rapid expansion on high school and college campuses nationwide.

"I want to make sure that it's something where our students that are currently in chapters, one day, their children will be chapter leaders or chapter members," Kirk told Fox News' Griff Jenkins.

Kirk gave the "Fox & Friends Weekend" co-host an exclusive tour of Turning Point USA's Arizona headquarters in a segment that aired Friday on "Fox & Friends," offering a behind-the-scenes look at the organization's growth and the spaces where she preserves her husband's memory.

INSIDE CHARLIE KIRK’S EFFORT TO DEVELOP THE NEXT GENERATION OF CONSERVATIVE VOICES

Kirk also discussed plans for a memorial beyond the existing tributes.

When asked whether she could envision building a presidential library-style tribute to her husband, Kirk said the organization was already considering the idea.

"It's on our list, and it's something that we have in the works," she said.

The proposed tribute would build on memorial displays already housed at Turning Point USA's headquarters, where Kirk has preserved handwritten letters and Bibles sent by supporters, along with personal items her husband left behind.

Among the reminders is Charlie Kirk's office, where notes remain on his desk and his chair sits empty.

CHARLIE KIRK STATUE BOUND FOR NY'S TIMES SQUARE AS SCULPTOR DEFIES THREATS AHEAD OF UNVEILING

"My kids are the only ones that sit in it," Kirk said.

Kirk also said her husband left behind outlines of his vision for Turning Point USA, which she said continues to guide the organization after his death.

"I'm just so blessed and grateful that Charlie left with us hundreds of his journals," she said. "He wrote down a lot about the future of Turning Point and the vision of Turning Point."

Turning Point USA says student involvement has increased as the organization expands its presence on high school and college campuses nationwide.

"Students were everything to Charlie," Kirk said.

"This was his mission ground, was to be able to touch the hearts and minds of the students, and he did that. And through our amazing team that we have, we're continuing to do that."

item.title: Thousands flood Brussels streets as anti-austerity protests erupt into clashes with police
item.description: Masked agitators clashed with riot police in Brussels as thousands of others marched against Belgium's austerity measures and cost of living crisis.
item.content:encoded:
Thousands of demonstrators poured into the streets of Brussels on Friday, at times clashing with police officers, to protest the Belgian government's budget-tightening measures and the overall rise in the cost of living.

Dozens of protesters, most of them young and dressed in black with masks over their faces, were seen throwing rocks and firecrackers at police at the central Brussels railway station, The Associated Press reported.

They also set several fires, with photos showing a man lighting an electric scooter ablaze.

MAY DAY PROTESTS ACROSS EUROPE AND ASIA TURN INTO ANTI-AMERICAN, ANTI-ISRAEL POLITICAL BATTLEGROUNDS

Riot police responded by deploying tear gas canisters and shooting water cannons, tactics that dispersed the crowds. The chaos in the streets contributed to increased traffic across the Belgian capital.

Police said the unrest was caused by people unaffiliated with the anti-austerity demonstration, which drew an estimated 30,000 participants, the AP reported.

Two of Belgium’s largest labor unions organized Friday’s daylong national strike, with a separate public-sector walkout planned for Monday. Union leaders also distanced themselves from the unrest, saying those responsible were not affiliated with their movement.

THINK YOUR STATE IS EXPENSIVE? NEW DATA REVEALS WHERE AMERICANS FACE THE HIGHEST COST-OF-LIVING

Union members and their supporters were dressed in red or green as they marched peacefully throughout the city.

Marie Gobert, a single mother and social worker, came to Brussels from Namur for the march, telling the AP she "cannot make ends meet."

The rising cost of schools, public transport and train tickets is what preoccupies her the most.

FRANCE ROCKED BY STUDENT RIOTS AS HUNDREDS ARRESTED, VIOLENCE SPREADS NATIONWIDE

"You can feel the social tension, you can feel anger starting to simmer everywhere," Gobert said. "The education system is being dismantled, and when young people want to speak out, no one listens to them."

This summer, Belgium’s French Community government raised standard university tuition by roughly 43% this academic year, from €835 to €1,194, as part of a broader austerity program.

In June, there were clashes between protesters and police in Brussels over dissatisfaction with the tuition hike and other issues with the French-language education system, including overcrowded classrooms and difficulty accessing study materials.

This week, hundreds of students took to the streets of the eastern Belgian city of Liège. Local media reported that 107 students were arrested.

The Associated Press and Reuters contributed to this report.

EL-SAYED'S SCATHING OBAMA CRITIQUE RESURFACES AHEAD OF JOINT CAMPAIGN RALLY

UNEARTHED SOCIAL MEDIA POSTS CONTRADICT EL-SAYED'S 'CAPITALIST' NARRATIVE

item.title: Jerry Jones slams table after Dak Prescott throws critical late interception in brutal Cowboys loss
item.description: Jerry Jones slammed the table after Dak Prescott's late interception sealed the Dallas Cowboys' shocking 24-16 home loss to the 0-4 Buccaneers.
item.content:encoded:
Watching his team lose in Primetime to a previously winless squad starting an undrafted rookie quarterback? Safe to say, Jerry Jones was not a happy camper on Thursday.

After Dak Prescott’s second interception of the game as the Dallas Cowboys were trying to mount a comeback late in the fourth quarter of their shocking 24-16 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Jones slammed his hand down on the table in his suite in obvious frustration.

The 83-year-old owner called the upset loss "very disappointing."

"I, of course, appreciated any chance we might have had there near the end," Jones told reporters after the game. "But the Buccaneers really took it to us. In my view, they did it inside. That’s where the real damage was done, we’ll see. That’s really surprising to me. That’s what it is, we missed a great opportunity here to build something, but they really all the way, probably most all the phases, they won it tonight.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"We had a chance maybe to pull it out at the end and that didn’t work for us. This is very disappointing, and I know it’s disappointing to our home crowd — it is to me."

Jones wasn’t the only member of the Cowboys visibly frustrated, as star wide receiver George Pickens slammed his helmet into the turf after Prescott’s late interception.

The Cowboys were down 24-10 with about eight and a half minutes left in the game when they rattled off a 10-play, 99-yard drive in just over three minutes. The drive concluded with Pickens making a leaping grab in the end zone to make it 24-16. The Cowboys went for the two-point conversion but did not convert.

The maligned Cowboys defense then forced the Bucs into a three-and-out on the next possession, setting up the offense with a chance to tie the game.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Prescott managed to drive the Cowboys into Buccaneers territory, getting to the 24-yard line with 1:30 left.

However, the comeback attempt was thwarted when Prescott’s pass went through tight end Jake Ferguson’s hands and off his helmet high into the Texas air. Buccaneers linebacker Alex Anzalone fell under the ball and snared it before it hit the AT&T Stadium turf.

The Cowboys still had all three timeouts, affording them an opportunity to get the ball back one last time, but Bucs running back Bucky Irving scampered for the game-sealing first down two plays later.

Irving’s run capped an impressive performance, as he ran for 165 yards on 21 carries and a touchdown while also catching two passes for 10 yards and a touchdown. His performance was essential for a team that started Jalon Daniels, an undrafted rookie making his second career start.

The Cowboys fell to 2-3 with the loss, and Jones wasn’t expecting his squad to be in this position.

"This isn’t fold the tents here. We are 2-3. We didn’t expect to be 2-3," Jones said. "We didn’t expect this. ... We didn’t expect this Tampa team to come in here 0-4, either."

The Cowboys’ next game will also come in Primetime, as they will look to bounce back when they play the Green Bay Packers next Sunday night.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.
